def: NVMe controller-level reset initiated by clearing CC.EN from 1 to 0. The host waits for CSTS.RDY to become 0; all I/O queues are deleted and outstanding commands are dropped without completions. AQA, ASQ and ACQ are not reset.
CAP bits 31:24: worst-case time, in 500 ms units, the host should wait for CSTS.RDY to change after it changes CC.EN.
NVMe 2.x register reporting separate ready timeouts for 'ready with media' and 'ready independent of media' controller ready modes. Confirm field layout in the Base specification.
Reset of every controller in an NVM subsystem, initiated by writing 4E564D65h ("NVMe") to the NSSR register at offset 20h when CAP.NSSRS = 1. On PCIe it commonly takes the link down.
CC bits 15:14: 01b requests a normal shutdown, 10b an abrupt shutdown, before power is removed.
CSTS bits 3:2: 00b normal operation, 01b shutdown processing occurring, 10b shutdown processing complete.
Identify Controller field giving the typical time, in microseconds, from a normal shutdown notification to shutdown complete; RTD3R is the matching resume latency.
SMART / Health log counter of power-ons that followed a power loss without a completed shutdown; key field evidence for platform power sequencing problems.
PCIe reset of a whole device and its link: Fundamental Reset (cold or warm) or Hot Reset. Resets all functions, configuration space and the NVMe controller.
Hardware-applied PCIe reset: cold (power cycle) or warm (PERST# asserted with power maintained).
In-band PCIe Conventional Reset signalled by the Hot Reset bit in TS1 ordered sets, usually triggered by setting Secondary Bus Reset in the bridge above the device.
Sideband reset signal from platform to device, defined by form-factor specifications; asserting it applies Fundamental Reset.

Reset of a single PCIe function via Initiate Function Level Reset in Device Control; the link and other functions are unaffected; configuration space and the NVMe controller of that function are reset.
Bridge Control bit that makes a Root Port or switch Downstream Port issue a Hot Reset to everything below it.

exp: Configuration Request Retry Status / Request Retry Status
def: Completion status (010b) a function returns to configuration requests while it is still initializing after reset; software retries. Renamed and generalized as RRS in the PCIe 6.0 era.
PCIe mechanism in which a Downstream Port takes its link down on a configured uncorrectable error to contain it; the device below experiences a reset-equivalent link down.
Uncorrectable Data Link Layer error reported by a Downstream Port when its link goes down without a prior orderly request.
Bit in the PCI Power Management Control/Status register; when 1, a D3hot to D0 transition preserves function state, so a PM-based reset does nothing.
Hardware-autonomous PCIe link power states (L0s, L1) entered when the link is idle while the device stays in D0; enabled through Link Control.
Deeper sub-states of the PCIe L1 link state that stop the reference clock (via CLKREQ#) and, in L1.2, common-mode voltages; L1.2 entry is gated by LTR.
PCIe message by which a device reports how much service latency it can tolerate, used by the platform to choose power states such as L1.2.
PCIe device power state with power maintained in which a function responds only to configuration requests; the link goes to L1.
PCIe device power state with main power removed; returning to D0 is a conventional reset.

NVMe feature (Feature Identifier 0Ch) in which the controller moves itself to a non-operational power state after an idle time, following a 32-entry host-supplied table (target state bits 7:3, idle ms bits 31:8).
32-byte Identify Controller entry describing one NVMe power state: maximum power, non-operational flag, entry/exit latency and relative performance.
NVMe power state in which the controller processes no I/O commands; an I/O submission returns it to an operational state, paying the exit latency.
Open-drain sideband signal used to stop and restart the PCIe reference clock for L1 PM Substates.
Time to return from a low-power state to full operation; PCIe link exit latencies are microseconds, NVMe non-operational exit latencies (EXLAT) often milliseconds, and they add up.
TLP attribute permitting a posted request or completion to pass earlier posted requests; enabled per function in Device Control. Safe on NVMe data writes, never on CQE or MSI-X writes.
TLP attribute permitting reordering between TLPs with different Requester (or Completer) IDs while keeping same-source order; enabled in Device Control 2.
Attribute telling the Root Complex a transaction need not be snooped against CPU caches; affects coherence/visibility, not ordering rules.
PCIe request that receives no completion: Memory Writes and Messages.
Programming model in which a producer writes data then a flag, and a consumer that observes the flag must observe the data; NVMe's data then CQE then MSI-X sequence relies on it.
3-bit TLP field selecting a traffic class mapped to a Virtual Channel; PCIe ordering rules apply only within a Traffic Class.
Completion header field: for memory read completions, the number of bytes remaining to complete the request, including the bytes in this completion.
Completion header field: bits 6:0 of the byte address of the first enabled byte returned in a memory read completion.
64 or 128 bytes; when a read is split, every completion except the last must end on a naturally aligned RCB boundary.
Requester-side timer per non-posted request and the uncorrectable error raised when it expires; ranges selected in Device Control 2.
Uncorrectable error logged when a completion matches no outstanding request, e.g. a late answer after a timeout or a misrouted completion.
3-bit completion field: 000b Successful Completion, 001b Unsupported Request, 010b Configuration/Request Retry Status, 100b Completer Abort.
Largest TLP data payload a function may send or must accept, set in Device Control; completions must not exceed it.
